extraction.name: WebWalkerQA
extraction.description: A bilingual benchmark for evaluating LLM web traversal and information-seeking over official websites across conference, organization, education, and game domains. It contains 680 QA pairs built from over 1373 webpages.
extraction.creator: Jialong Wu, Wenbiao Yin, Yong Jiang, Zhenglin Wang, Zekun Xi, Runnan Fang, Linhai Zhang, Yulan He, Deyu Zhou, Pengjun Xie, Fei Huang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed in a two-stage funnel annotation strategy. First, official websites were traversed recursively to collect sub-links and subpages. GPT-4o was used to generate synthetic QA pairs from the collected page information. Second, crowd-sourced human annotators rewrote and calibrated the questions and answers and performed quality control and filtering to refine the final results.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Root official websites and their accessible sub-links/subpages from conference, organization, education, and game domains; official websites were initially identified through Google search using keywords such as "conference official website" or "game official website" and manually filtered.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Synthetic queries were generated from page information and specified roles; queries were verified and filtered to retain legitimate natural-language QA pairs with short entity answers; human annotators rewrote and calibrated questions and answers for correctness and consistency.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Only QA pairs with short answers containing entities were retained; illegitimate queries and unnatural phrasing were filtered out; human quality control was applied to refine the final dataset.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: GPT-4o performed initial annotation to generate synthetic QA pairs. Human annotators then rewrote and calibrated the questions and answers, and conducted quality control and filtering. For multi-source data, annotators generated queries requiring information from at least two sublinks and verified them with strict QA verification. For single-source data, annotators verified that the answer required current knowledge from doc2 and was concise and correct.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A strict verification step was used to judge whether a query-answer pair truly required combining two documents for multi-source data or required doc2 for single-source data. The paper emphasizes filtering for concise entity answers and rejecting cases that could be answered from one document or were not natural queries.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Crowd-sourced human annotators; no further demographic details are provided.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset currently comprises 680 high-quality QA pairs, which the authors note is limited due to the complexity of web-agent queries. The paper also mentions approximately 14k silver QA pairs that are not yet human-verified. The benchmark uses only HTML-DOM and clickable buttons, leaving visual modalities for future work.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating LLMs and web agents on web traversal, information-seeking QA, and multi-step reasoning; used for testing performance and efficiency, and for comparing RAG systems and agent frameworks. The paper also discusses potential use for training/fine-tuning agentic systems, but the benchmark itself is primarily for evaluation.
